checks.label: The idea is to get a line that has equal numbers of points on either side, and the line may not pass through many of them: the line laid through the winding's readings has as many above it as below and passes through none

By hand: R = 0.04T + 10 leaves 4 above and 4 below, no stick over 0.2 Ω; the opening line R = 0.04T + 11 has all 8 below it; pinned, R = 0.26T still splits them 4 and 4, yet its sticks are 7.9 Ω at 10 °C and 7.5 Ω at 80 °C, all 4 above on the left

The lay-it Check passes exactly when 4 sit above and 4 below with no stick over 0.4 Ω: the line through the middle passes, the opening line fails, a line tilted to 0.05 Ω per °C fails on its long sticks though it splits them 4 and 4, and a gentler 0.0375 passes

In many materials the dependence of resistance on temperature is approximately linear and can be modelled using a linear equation: every example winding reading sits close to one straight line, its stick far shorter than the line's rise across the readings

Read off the line at 20 °C and 70 °C: 12.8 − 10.8 = 2.0 Ω over 50 °C gives 0.04 Ω per °C, and c = 10.8 − 0.04 × 20 = 10.0 Ω; dragged anywhere along the line, the two points give the same gradient and the same c
Read to within 0.1 Ω, the line at 40 and 50 °C allows 0.02 to 0.06 Ω per °C, at 20 and 70 °C only 0.036 to 0.044, so the far pair's fan is the narrower; spread wider still, it narrows further

Provided that the limit of proportionality is not exceeded, a graph of stretching force against extension is a straight line through the origin: the spring's line passes through the origin, is laid only through readings before the limit, and the readings past it fall below the line

The gradient of the graph of force (y-axis) and extension (x-axis) is numerically equal to the spring constant: on the spring screens force is up the side and extension along, and the gradient comes out in newtons per millimetre, named the spring constant

The law of a straight line graph is of the form y = ax + b: the lifting machine's law is written P = aW + b, with a the step triangle's rise over its run and b where the line, carried back, meets the effort axis

Every answer offered is written from its own numbers: the right one is worked from the screen's own line, and each wrong one is a real slip (two readings, run over rise, the line pinned through zero, the first reading taken as c, the bent part, or through zero from the last reading)
Which line fits: A leaves 6 above and none below; B leaves 3 and 3 but all 3 above sit on the left; C leaves 3 and 3 spread along it, with the shortest sticks
Which two points: the line far apart allows the narrowest range of gradients, the line close together a range five times as wide, and two readings give 0.08 Ω per °C, twice the line's
Before an answer a puzzle keeps back its working, triangle, intercept and fans; a right answer or Why? draws them; each wrong pick has a hint of its own, and a slip that can be drawn is drawn dashed
Every stick runs straight up or down from its reading to the line, and the count above the graph matches the sticks drawn, wherever the handles are dragged
The through-zero switch pins the line at the origin: on, the line's c is 0 and one handle swings it; off, both handles are back on the line through the middle
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 2.8 to 5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; a puzzle's drawing finishes within 2.5 s
